understanding: F uses signed force addition in one declared frame and a=F_net/m for m>0, so acceleration carries the net-force sign.
U represents the same positive physical length in a larger unit; divide the numerical millimetre value by 1000 using 1000 mm = 1 m.

assignment.method: Read only the issued brief and exact BP-1 file; verify the BP-1 byte SHA-256. Record any relevant prior exposure before authoring. Invent one clear setting and value set per profile without benchmark access. For F, stipulate positive mass, two opposing horizontal forces, the positive axis and no other horizontal forces; ask both net force and signed acceleration; assign force signs, add them, then divide by positive mass using F_net=m*a and state units. For U, choose a positive millimetre length under a physically ordinary premise; ask conversion and why 1000; derive L_m=L_mm/1000 from 1000 mm=1 m. Write both self-contained prompts and solutions. Independently recalculate your own values by hand or Python; for F reverse the coordinate convention and check the signs reverse with magnitudes unchanged, and for U check converting back returns the same length. These are self-checks, not additional exercises. Read back both files; report actual tools/results and part-level evidence as SELF-ASSESSED. Do not infer independent validity or learning.
